data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Opinion, advice, politeness and modal nuance
learningPoints: Develops nuanced use of modal verbs for advice and probability.
Strengthens opinion expression in speaking tests.
Prepares you for real-world English use beyond the classroom.
ESOL B2 and aligns with IELTS 6.0–6.5 and TOEFL iBT 72–94 score ranges.

sections.explain: 'Must' expresses a confident deduction + base verb: 'must be busy'. No 'to' or '-s' after a modal.

words.word: She isn't answering; she musts be busy.
She isn't answering; she must be busy.
She isn't answering; she must to be busy.
The results might improve next year.
The results must improve next year (certainty).
The results might improves next year.

sections.explain: For a negative deduction use 'can't be': 'they can't be at home'. 'mustn't' means prohibition, and modals take no 'to'.

words.word: The lights are off; they mustn't be at home.
The lights are off; they can't to be at home.
The lights are off; they can't be at home.

sections.explain: 'Might' expresses possibility + base verb: 'might be'. No 'to' or '-ing' after 'might'.

words.word: He might be stuck in traffic.
He might being stuck in traffic.
He might to be stuck in traffic.

sections.summary: 'Can't' to reject a claim as impossible.
sections.explain: 'Can't be' rejects something as impossible: 'That can't be true'. Modals aren't used with 'do' ('doesn't can'), and the adjective is 'true', not 'truly'.

words.word: That doesn't can be true; I don't believe it.
That can't be truly; I don't believe it.
That can't be true; I don't believe it.

sections.explain: 'May' + base verb expresses possibility: 'may know'. No '-ing' or 'to' after 'may'.

words.word: They may to know the answer already.
They may know the answer already.
They may knowing the answer already.

sections.summary: 'Must have' + participle for a past deduction.
sections.explain: 'Must have' + past participle deduces about the past: 'must have rained'. 'must have rain' lacks the participle, and 'must has' is wrong.

words.word: The road is wet; it must have rained.
The road is wet; it must has rained.
The road is wet; it must have rain.

sections.explain: 'Could' expresses possibility + base verb: 'could be'. No 'to' or '-ing' after 'could'.

words.word: She could be at the library.
She could to be at the library.
She could being at the library.
This decision could affect many employees.
This decision could affects many employees.
This decision must affect many employees (certainty).

sections.explain: Using modal verbs carefully expresses balanced opinion.

words.word: While the plan may be expensive, it could bring long-term benefits.
While the plan is expensive but it could bring benefits.
While the plan may be expensive it will bring benefits certainly.
